source_refs.note: Topic 1.3, printed pages 3-4: metals, non-metals, metalloids and the stair-step line. Figure 1.1 (the printed periodic table) is carried by the schematic original.

blocks.text: Elements can be broadly classified as metals, non-metals and metalloids. Metals tend to lose electrons to form positive ions; iron, copper, gold and silver are examples. Non-metals tend to gain electrons to form negative ions; chlorine, sulfur and phosphorus are examples. The metalloids separate the metals and non-metals on the periodic table and exhibit some properties of each.

Most periodic tables carry a stair-step line that identifies these groups. The line begins at boron (B) and extends down to polonium (Po), taking in Si, Ge, As, Sb and Te. Elements to the left of the line are metals; elements just to its right show properties of both metals and non-metals and are the metalloids or semimetals; elements at the far right are non-metals. The exception is hydrogen, the first element of the table.
